answer: Latent-key beacon binding: each identity embeds a distinct umber-tinted pigment signature derived from its secret key, published as a fixed-width bit pattern. Agents must periodically emit their beacon; a duplicated identity running two instances produces divergent timing offsets that a shared ledger records as a ridge of conflicting signatures. Detection is self-revealing because honest copies cannot synchronize without colluding, and collusion exposes the key. Attacker cost: one fresh beacon key per instance plus continuous re-derivation work, so N sybils pay N times the beacon maintenance.
